messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT — gpu-serve-usw queue depth > 90% (avg 3400 reqs), per-shard throttle engaged, recent spike detected at 2024-04-12T14:12:34Z. autoscaler attempted growth but hit pool credit limit. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/dashboard/db/gpu-serve

sre_oncall_jun: seeing it, joining. queue growth started ~14:10. p95 latency jumping. any deployments around then?

ashley_devex: rolling canary for continuous-batching tweak landed at 14:05 in dedicated-usw. small param change: batch_window_ms from 20->35 and prefix_cache_ttl from 600->30 (intended to reduce stale prefixes).

raj_infra: oh — prefix_cache_ttl -> 30s? that's huge for churned workloads. could cause missstorm. also cluster-level fairshare credits drop for dedicated pools this morning (maintenance). autoscaler logs show "scale denied: credit_exhausted"

elaine_runtime: confirmed logs:
```
[14:12:18] kvcache: prefix miss rate 87% (was 12% at 14:00)
[14:12:19] batching: mean batch size fell 42%
[14:12:20] serve: per-token qps drop -> more outstanding requests -> queue grows
[14:12:22] autoscaler: requested +32 gpus, granted 0 (credit_limit)
```

ops_lead_marta: customer impact? any 5xx/denials?

ashley_devex: a few tenants on dedicated-usw seeing 429 throttles and streaming disconnects. I count ~12 tenants with repeated 429s since 14:11. No 500s yet.

sre_oncall_jun: immediate mitigation plan: 1) roll back continuous-batching canary to previous params 2) bump prefix_cache_ttl back to 600s on canaries 3) request manual credit override or emergency allocation while rollback completes

raj_infra: filing manual allocation now — raising to infra with priority override (ticket #INC-5412). If override takes >5m, we'll evict non-critical background pools to free credits.

deploybot: Deploy triggered by ashley_devex: rollback continuous-batching-canary -> v1.4.3 (jobs: canary group A,B). ETA 2m.

elaine_runtime: rolling back config on the runtime side now. patch: set batch_window_ms=20, continuous_batching_enabled=true (previous), prefix_cache_ttl=600. applying to 20% canary first.

sre_oncall_jun: while rollback running, enable temporary throttle escape hatch: route critical tenant traffic to dedicated-hotspot pool with reserved capacity (hard limit) to avoid 429s. Command: `routectl move --tenant=critical-tenants --pool=hotspot-usw --force`

ashley_devex: moved 4 critical tenants. Verified streams restored for two tenants. Still seeing queue decrease but slowly.

raj_infra: manual allocation approved by infra oncall. applied +16 GPUs to dedicated-usw. Credit counter now at - but flagged for postmortem.

ops_lead_marta: good—please capture timeline and customer list for post-incident message. Also estimate RTO for affected tenants.

elaine_runtime: metrics update: prefix miss rate falling after rollback step completed at 14:18. mean batch size recovering. queue depth down to 1200 at 14:20. p95 latency trending down from 2200ms -> 540ms by 14:22.

sre_oncall_jun: retaining elevated logging for 1h. Will circulate short incident note. Need one-off followups: 1) revert unintended prefix_ttl change in config templates 2) validate canary gating for batching params to include throughput test 3) review credit accounting for reserved pools to avoid future auto-deny

ashley_devex: root cause summary draft: inadvertent canary config changed prefix cache TTL and batching window, causing high prefix eviction -> missstorm -> smaller batch sizes -> reduced throughput -> queue growth. Autoscaler attempted to grow but was limited by maintenance-era credit accounting; both factors compounded.

deploybot: rollback finished across canaries at 14:18:58. CI logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/48721

raj_infra: credit override will be reconciled by finance/infrastructure. Creating follow-up RFC to add emergency quota pool that autoscaler can draw from during credit maintenance windows.

ops_lead_marta: customer comms: prepare a concise note with impacted tenants + times (14:10-14:22 degraded, rollbacks complete 14:19). call this "service degradation due to batching/cache regression and allocation limit". Ashley can you draft and I will review?

ashley_devex: drafting now. Will include mitigation steps, ETA on billing reconciliation, and steps we're taking to prevent recurrence.

elaine_runtime: saving relevant traces: trace ids list: [trc-98721, trc-98722, trc-98723] and logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/1718205555/

sre_oncall_jun: handing off to raj for infra followups. I'm keeping watch for 30m then will mark incident as resolved if metrics remain stable. @raj_infra you'll own postmortem and follow-up RFCs.

raj_infra: ack. prepping postmortem template and will include timeline, config diff, autoscaler decision logs, and credit accounting. assigning actions: (A1) template rollback guard for canaries, (A2) emergency credit pool RFC, (A3) alerting change: raise early signal for prefix miss spikes at >30%

ops_lead_marta: noted. closing the live pager. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: NOTICE — incident state changed to mitigated by sre_oncall_jun at 2024-04-12T14:25:55Z. Severity reduced to P2. If metrics regress, pager will re-open.

ashley_devex: quick note: the config change was a copy/paste mistake in canary manifest — added checklists to PR template to prevent TTL overrides without an eval.

elaine_runtime: final stats snapshot at 14:30: p95 latency 430ms, queue depth 200, prefix miss rate 9%, batch size at 86% of normal. No further client 429 spikes detected.

sre_oncall_jun: leaving a short blameless note in #postmortems channel and scheduling a 1hr follow-up with infra + devex tomorrow to run through forced credit scenario tests.

raj_infra: creating INC-5412 follow-ups: RFC-998: emergency-autoscale-pool; TASK-1112: canary-e2e-throughput; TASK-1113: prefix-ttl-guard.

ops_lead_marta: thanks team. Good mitigation and communication.

pagerbot: Thread closed by sre_oncall_jun at 1718206155."
